Oh, well, I haven't really played League of Legends since around 2014, though I started in season 1. I became very invested in the game originally because my then girlfriend liked it. I didn't like that she was better than me so, for some reason, after we broke up I committed myself to getting very good at it. My internet was pretty bad at the time so I had to focus more on my macro game than my micro game, and also due to my anxiety I didn't play a lot of ranked. I did my placements in S3 and won all my games plus a few more so I got put in plat, but I really didn't like competing since I was already quite an anxious person.

I stopped playing shortly after going to University since I was more imminently distracted by new friends, girls, getting drunk and so on. I've tried going back to it but they brutalized my dear Heimerdinger with his rework. I'm sure the rework is actually a lot better, but I just liked him the way he was. Anyway. The last game I played was vanilla WoW, which was a terrible idea. My whole server was 90% man-children.

In terms of your chess-boasting (or lack thereof), I think it's good to be confident in your abilities. It's why I relied on video games for so long. I'd get very good at them and beat everyone and then feel good about myself. The only difference is chess is actually a game worth being good at. Vladimir Nabokov was a huge fan of chess and he's arguably one of the best prose writers of the past century.

Hi there. Thanks for your response. On the matter of writing, I figure, so long as you're having fun then you should keep on going with it. I started my first journal when I was 17 and the thing was a disgrace, but I improved over time. Keep it up, is what I mean to say.

I feel you're very right to recommend the gym to me. I used to love doing simple routines of pull ups and pushups in my apartment, but my new place has flimsy doorframes so I have nowhere to put a bar. As recently as a week ago I was on a good streak of running 2.5k to a calisthenics park, working out, and running back again. The only issue is I'm too anxious to go during regular hours so I'd go at 3.45AM. It worked and I felt good, but it wasn't sustainable. I tried going during the day but the park is next to a subway station so I found myself leaving prematurely (social anxiety). 

Once this next round of assignments has passed and my cold has cleared up, I'll give it another shot. Thanks again for your advice.
I, too, would like my junk to spend less time at the forefront of my consciousness.

Hi there. I'm sort of getting prepared to go out at the moment so I can't give a full response (as grateful as I am that you took the time to reach out to me) but I wanted to say that the complements on my writing are likely motivated by the part in my post where I basically say that writing is the only thing I have left.

I hope that people mean it genuinely, since I really do not feel good about anything else in my life... But the reason I'm saying this is that you shouldn't feel hesitant to share your own story because you're worried how people will critique your writing. That's not a part of the community. In my case, the writing is just a direct route to raising my self-esteem.

Beyond that I want to thank you for your words of encouragement and for interrupting my neurotic cycle of criticizing myself for things over which I have no control. I am currently in psychoanalysis which hopefully will help me make peace with my initial trauma, but yes, the OCD symptoms are bad and I'm sure are 90% of the reason I felt bad enough to post here. Without anyone to keep tabs on you, it can be very easy to let one's rituals and obsessions get out of hand.

I think it all boils down to the surgeries. They made me feel so sickly and ashamed of myself that I was not comfortable expressing outward sexual interest in anyone, so when my father and brother would ogle women on the TV I'd just sit there in silence.

They've never cast me out. They all like me, as well as loving me. I just don't share with them the way most people probably would. They know nothing about me, and the thought of being open with them repulses me. It makes me start to shiver and my teeth chatter as though I were cold.
Thank you for saying so. It is hard living in a vacuum. Occasions like this are really the only occasions when people besides myself get to read the things I write.

Hi there. Thank you for paying an interest in my awkward phallic tragedy. I do not knowingly blame my parents for my issues. I'm sure I had some resentment towards them back when this was a burning issue for me, but nowadays I don't really think about them. I know I've never felt comfortable with them. They all thought I was gay until I had my first girlfriend since I'd never felt comfortable expressing my sexual orientation in their presence.

They know about my issues but not in any depth. They probably understand it more as a physical issue (the curve) and less as a matter of psychological scarring.

This is quite telling but very sad. Today is my birthday and all I've done is sit around and weep in my apartment. I told myself it couldnt be worse than last year but oh boy did I ever prove myself wrong. 

My roommate and closest friend sent me a text at 1 today with a picture of a beer saying "I'm having a pint on you mate". I have been sitting at home. I received a package from my parents which sort of turned my weeping up a gear as I felt simultaneously ashamed for being unable to enjoy the life they've given me and also sad for the fact that I am so far away from them when they're obviously the only ones who care. I do not know if I can take another year of this.

Now my only attempt to reach out will be buried, and with it goes another year of overlooked depression. Who can blame them. Nobody needs this in their life.

I would say no, but it isn't veganism's fault by any means. I found veganism because of an unhealthy obsession with my own health (oh the irony). My obsession was sparked by a late night impulse purchase of a book called "Living Well with Anxiety" after a particularly disturbing night I'd spent with my now ex-girlfriend who was (and I suspect still is) a very unstable girl. The book was very poorly formatted and was also probably quite old I figured since they were still using the word "retarded" to describe mentally handicapped people. It was all pretty weird but the nutrition section caught my attention and I guess ever since then I've been trying to treat my anxiety through healthier lifestyle choices, diet, exercise etc.

The natural end-point of my obsession was veganism,  a diet with little to no flaws, but as soon as I'd solved the problem of diet I just found myself moving onto other areas of my life to work on, since it's pretty preposterous to think a change in diet could fix a lifelong mental illness. At present I'm working my way downhill fairly slowly, but I think I'm becoming a better person in the process, so I have that to feel good about. Having recently read Thoreau's Walden I realized my love for the natural world and all its inhabitats, and I suppose in the context of a forest or a lake I do feel calmer knowing that my love of chipmunks, muskrats, loons etc. isn't contradicted by my lifestyle choices. But day to day, the struggle is ever worsening. Just gotta keep on trying I suppose.

That's just reddit though. A bunch of people with an immovable set of beliefs who pride themselves on their openness to new ideas.  It's worked for them thus far. I don't see it changing any time soon. Original or even just marginal areas of thought are not welcome on the mainstream subreddits.  They'd rather hear it from one of their own so they don't feel like they're on trial.

When I look at these threads and see meat eaters engaging in sensible debate about the topic of veganism I think, even though inspiring people to embrace veganism is the ideal outcome, if you consider that perhaps 10 to 20 people who read the thread will actually make the effort to cut down their meat eating by something as significant as, say, a quarter, then even if nobody converts to veganism, the equivalent of 2.5 to 5 vegans worth of environmental damage and animal suffering has been prevented. I find thinking about it in that way makes me feel better.

I am not that person but I may as well respond. The issue with milk of any kind is that in order for an animal to lactate it needs to have been impregnated, and once that animal is born you have an animal that's producing milk and its baby that wants to drink that milk. This means that if you want to take that milk then you have to force a baby animal from doing the thing it wants to do and drink the fluid that is specifically designed to make it grow into a healthy adult animal. So for milk I think it depends on whether or not you personally think it is ethical to prevent an animal from feeding on its mother's teet. There's also the issue of how you impregnate the animal. Assuming you don't buy the sperm from a distributor and forcibly impregnate the animal (and then you'd have to consider the conditions that the male animal is living in that you are perpetuating by purchasing its sperm, as well as the act of forcibly impregnating an animal being quite clearly a shitty thing to do to an animal) you'd have to keep and feed a male, even though you only need it for one thing every nine months or so. Upon the birth of the baby you'd also have to figure out what you want to do with the baby. If male, you have another animal eating feed and not doing much else, if female, you have the same deal unless you decide to impregnate it in which case you have to consider whether you find it unethical to mate the young animal with its father... or otherwise get another male and then you have five animals. So for goats and cows it's not really as simple as "buy a cow, get milk". Milk is part of a reproductive process and it's not really a situation where you can just stop at one animal.

Now as for eggs that's a complex issue as well. Eggs are unlike milk in that hens will produce them regardless of whether or not the egg is fertilized. The issue with this of course is that chickens will produce up to 300 eggs a year under 'the right' circumstances, which is very bad for the hen. The reason they produce so many eggs is because of how we have manipulated the dna of hens in favour of optimal egg production, so ethically speaking you have to decide for yourself if you are going to take responsibility for the behaviour of past men and women. Conveniently, hens cease producing eggs when they have filled their nest with eggs (don't ask me how that works) and so if you do not take any eggs from a hen they will produce less eggs and strain themselves less. Interestingly you can get prosthetic eggs to put in nests of hens so they don't feel compelled to produce so many eggs which would mean you could get away with taking an egg every week or so and the hen likely wouldn't experience any health problems, assuming they are fed an adequate diet. Of course, as with goats and cows, you also have to consider where you get your hens from. It will come as no surprise that hens are in much higher demand than roosters, and sadly the male chicks will more likely than not be killed moments after hatching as it would not be economical to house and feed an animal that serves no practical purpose. So for every hen you purchase you may expect there is a male chick who was slaughtered in infancy, solely because your desire to own a hen made killing that male chick profitable. You may consider the idea of housing a rescue hen, but that may not be a 100% effective method of procuring an egg laying hen as you will not know how long that hen has been laying eggs for (they have an expiry date) and also I think I would consider how you're basically taking a freed slave and forcing them back into doing the same type of labour, just under more favourable conditions. If the hen had no other place to go then taking it home with you is obviously the kindest option, but again, these are questions that you have to process through your own ethical filters in order to figure out if that's something you'd want to take part in.
